title: The Final Parish
premise: True-crime podcaster Lena Iversen has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidental, and when a confession letter arrives postmarked the day after a fourth victim's funeral, she realizes the killer isn't taunting her — he's recruiting her. The letter's author is Father Anselm Rook, the parish priest who once mentored her late brother, and he claims the four 'accidents' were executions of men who destroyed evidence in a decades-old drowning case. As Lena investigates, she discovers her brother was involved too, forcing her to choose between exposing a killer she's come to understand or burying the truth to protect his memory. In the end, Lena traps Rook at the tidal causeway where the original drowning occurred, records his full confession as the tide rises, and must decide whether justice means a courtroom or the sea.
about_author: Cyrus Coldharbour spent fifteen years as a court reporter in coastal New England before turning to fiction, a career that left him fluent in the gap between what the law proves and what actually happened. He writes from a converted boathouse, where the tide schedule dictates his working hours.

chapters.title: Postmarked the Day After
chapters.summary: Lena Iversen receives an anonymous confession letter describing a death only the killer could know, postmarked the day after Harold Voss's funeral. Her POV establishes her obsessive method and the three cold cases she's quietly cracked. The emotional beat: the thrill of being seen by someone dangerous.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Pattern
chapters.summary: Lena reviews her private files on the three 'accidental' deaths she solved, finding each victim connected to St. Brigid's Parish. She visits Voss's widow, who reveals Voss burned papers the week he died. The beat: dread crystallizing into certainty that a fourth case has begun.

chapters.title: The Priest Who Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: Lena confronts Father Anselm Rook at St. Brigid's; he is calm, courteous, and quotes her own podcast back at her. A second letter arrives that evening, this one naming her brother Daniel. The beat: the hunter realizing she's inside the trap.

chapters.title: What Daniel Left Behind
chapters.summary: In flashback-tinged present scenes, Lena searches her estranged brother's abandoned storage unit after his overdose two years prior, finding a parish photo and a torn page from a 1987 coroner's report. The beat: grief reopening as a live wound.

chapters.title: The Drowned Boy of Greywater Point
chapters.summary: Lena digs into the original case: sixteen-year-old Tomas Reyes, drowned off the tidal causeway in 1987, ruled misadventure. Detective Marcus Hale, her reluctant former ally, warns her off but slips her the old file. The beat: the past acquiring weight and teeth.

chapters.title: Four Names, One List
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing the victims against the 1987 file, Lena finds all four served on the parish search party that 'failed' to find Tomas. A fifth name remains: Daniel Iversen. The beat: vertigo as her family enters the frame.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Draft
chapters.summary: Rook sends a longer letter admitting the killings in clinical detail but framing them as sacrament, inviting Lena to 'hear the whole mass.' She realizes he wants a witness, not absolution. The beat: horrified fascination warring with duty.

chapters.title: Hale's Cold Case
chapters.summary: Detective Hale's POV: he suspects Lena is either hunting the killer or protecting him, and reopens the file officially, putting her under quiet surveillance. Their tense alliance frays. The beat: loyalty beginning to cost something real.

chapters.title: The Widow's Testimony
chapters.summary: Voss's widow gives Lena a hidden tape: the four men confessing on camera in 1990 to covering up what really happened to Tomas — they saw him alive and walked away. The beat: moral ground shifting under Lena's feet.

chapters.title: Sacrament of Silence
chapters.summary: Lena secretly meets Rook in the empty church. He explains the cover-up, Daniel's role in destroying the tape's original, and why he waited for her specifically. She leaves without agreeing to anything — but without refusing. The beat: complicity taking root.

chapters.title: The Fifth Letter
chapters.summary: A letter arrives revealing Daniel didn't die of an overdose alone: Rook was there, holding his hand, and let him choose. Lena spirals, unsure whether to hate him or thank him. The beat: rage and gratitude fused into something unbearable.

chapters.title: Tail Lights on Chapel Road
chapters.summary: Hale follows Lena to a dead-drop and confronts her; she lies about the letters, burning their trust. That night someone searches her apartment — not Rook. The beat: paranoia multiplying the cast of threats.

chapters.title: The Sixth Name
chapters.summary: Lena identifies a living sixth member of the search party: Councilman Edric Mowbray, who has been obstructing the investigation through city hall. Mowbray offers her money for the tape. The beat: corruption wearing a respectable face.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: At Greywater Point at low tide, Lena finds physical evidence in the silt — Tomas's missing shoe buckle — proving he struggled, proving murder. Someone watches her from the dunes. The beat: the land itself becoming witness.

chapters.title: Mowbray's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Mowbray's POV chapter reveals he hired a fixer years ago and now fears Rook's list ends with him. He orders surveillance on both Lena and the priest. The beat: the predator discovering he is prey.

chapters.title: Broken Seal
chapters.summary: The fixer ransacks St. Brigid's for the tape; Rook is injured defending it and hospitalized. Lena arrives to find the rectory torn apart and a police cruiser outside. The beat: the game turning violent and public.

chapters.title: Two Truths in a Hospital Room
chapters.summary: Lena and Hale finally compare everything — letters, tape, file — and realize Rook engineered the entire collision to force official reckoning with the 1987 case. Hale must choose between procedure and justice. The beat: alliance rebuilt on shared heresy.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Rook, discharged, sends his final letter: meet me at the causeway at slack tide tomorrow, bring the tape, bring your judgment. Lena understands he intends to end it there, one way or another. The beat: terrible clarity before the storm.

chapters.title: Slack Water
chapters.summary: Climax part one: at the causeway, Rook confesses fully on Lena's recorder — the killing, the mercy, Daniel's last hours. Mowbray and the fixer arrive to silence them all. The beat: truth spoken aloud at last, and immediately endangered.

chapters.title: The Rising Tide
chapters.summary: Climax part two: violence on the causeway as the tide cuts it off. Hale intervenes; the fixer is lost to the water; Mowbray is arrested on the recording's strength. Rook walks toward the rising sea and Lena must stop him — or not. The beat: the choice the whole book has built toward.

chapters.title: Verdict Outside the Courtroom
chapters.summary: Resolution: Rook stands trial; Lena publishes the series, naming every name including Daniel's. Hale closes the 1987 case properly. At Tomas Reyes's grave, Lena leaves the shoe buckle and finally grieves her brother. The beat: costly, imperfect peace.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The Empty Pew
chapters.summary: Months later, Lena receives one last envelope — blank except for a single line: 'The parish is yours now.' She looks at her microphone, then out at the grey water, and begins recording. The beat: inheritance, vigilance, and the story continuing beyond the last page.
